get.description: One entry per scan round (`round` = lifecycle round: 0 is the initial scan, each rescan adds one), newest first, cursor-paginated (at most 20 rounds per page): status, aggregate verdict (`clean`, `spam`, `suspicious`, `malicious`, `unknown`, `timeout`, `error`; null while running), reason codes, required engines, the deadline, the SPF/DKIM/DMARC/ARC results and per engine its final result (outcome, score, threshold, action, reason codes, symbols with bounded options, engine and settings versions) and every attempt (failed attempts are retried and listed with their error code). The `attachment` engine entry lists its per-attachment results (step 4.2): part index, sanitized filename, declared and detected type, size, SHA-256, verdict, reason codes, the ClamAV signature and versions, YARA rule matches, archive inspection counts and findings (by entry index path, never names), a known-hash hit and the sandbox submission. The content cache is shared across organizations, so its hit/miss outcome is never shown, and the `attachment` engine reports no durations and second-granular times. The `bec` engine entry (step 4.4) carries its explainable verdict: versions, deterministic and final verdict and score, thresholds, input states, the fired rules with structured evidence (span offsets, never text), applied and shadow AI assessments (no response hashes or durations) and feedback references; `scanId` of a round is the id the BEC feedback route takes. The `dlp` engine entry (step 4.5) carries its masked result (versions, verdict, action, coverage detail, category aggregates, findings with masked samples only, the policy match and applied exceptions as public ids, the evidence state) **only for callers also holding `dlp:read`**; otherwise `dlp` is null and only the standard engine fields are shown. Matched values are never shown here: decrypted evidence is only in the audited `GET /messages/{messageId}/scans/{scanId}/dlp-evidence`. Each round lists its stored risk scores in `risk` (step 5.1; revision 0 = the round, 1 = with the late sandbox result): score 0–1000, level, verdict, recommended action, hard blocks, contributions by signal and group, engine evidence, trust decision, explanation and every version (profile public ids only); `[]` while running. Step 5.1 recommends and does not enforce (policy, step 5.2, decides); the default weights and thresholds are not validated detection accuracy. Each round carries its stored policy evaluation in `policy` (step 5.2; null while not evaluated): disposition, decisive rule, actions with their status (`enforced`, `requested`, `recorded`, `not_applicable`), floor, recommendation, explanation and hashes (ids and codes only; the full list per message is `GET /messages/{messageId}/policy-evaluations`). From the read replica: a round that just completed may still show as running. Symbol options can contain addresses or URLs of the message; filenames are attacker-controlled text.

info.title: Email Security Gateway API
info.description:
Control-plane API of the Email Security Gateway. Every business route is under `/api/v1` (ADR-0015, ADR-0053); nothing else is public. Probes (`/health/live`, `/health/ready`) and the Prometheus scrape (`/metrics`) are internal endpoints of the api port, never routed by the Ingress and not part of this document; this document itself (`/docs`, `/docs-json`) is served outside production only.

**Authentication.** A bearer access token (`Authorization: Bearer <JWT>`, from `POST /api/v1/auth/login`) or, where an operation lists the `api-key` scheme, an organization API key (`X-API-Key`). The organization is always the caller’s (the token or key), never a header or a body field; another tenant’s resource answers `404`. `x-eg-permissions` names the permission(s) each operation requires.

**Conventions (ADR-0050).** Resources are plural kebab-case nouns; a single resource is returned bare, a collection as `{ "data": [...], "nextCursor": string | null }` (the quarantine lists of step 5.3 keep `items`). Every error is `{ statusCode, error, code, message, correlationId, requestId, ... }` with a stable snake_case `code`; every response carries `X-Request-Id` (server-minted) and `x-correlation-id`. Request bodies and query strings are strict: an unknown field is `400 validation_failed`.

**Lists (ADR-0051).** `limit` (1-100, default 25) and `cursor`; keyset order, no totals, no offsets. Lists added in 6.1 (`x-eg-cursor: v1`) use signed cursors bound to the organization, the filters and the sort (`400 cursor_invalid` otherwise); earlier lists keep their unsigned `v0` cursors. A page may be short, even empty, while `nextCursor` is not null (scan budget): follow `nextCursor` until it is null. Filters are `field=value`, `field=a,b` and `field.gte=` / `.lte=` / `.gt=` / `.lt=`; `sort=-receivedAt` style.

**Rate limits and idempotency (ADR-0052).** Authenticated requests are limited per user or API key and per organization (60 s windows; `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, `RateLimit-Reset`); `x-eg-rate-class: sensitive | expensive` operations have their own tighter bucket. `429 rate_limited` carries `scope` and `Retry-After`; when the limiter store is down the API answers `503` (fail closed). Operations with `x-eg-idempotency` require an `Idempotency-Key` header (`required`: exactly once with the effect; `legacy`: the reservation interceptor, at most once per key); replays carry `Idempotency-Replayed: true`. Responses that contain a secret (`x-eg-returns-secret`) are never stored and take no key, except the two webhook secret routes (`x-eg-secret-replay: redacted`, ADR-0057): they require a key, store the response with `secret: null` and return the secret only in the original response.

**Integration surfaces today.** Organization API keys (`/api/v1/api-keys`, scoped to tenant permissions) for this API, SMTP connectors (`/api/v1/smtp-connectors`) for outbound relay from customer systems, and signed webhooks (`/api/v1/webhooks`, step 6.2) for mail, threat, quarantine and domain events.

**Not offered, by design.** `delivery_routes` management: no service reads that table (inbound destinations are `/domains/{id}/destinations`, outbound relay is SMTP connectors), so a management API would change nothing. Tenant-managed threat indicators and IP/domain/URL reputation: no engine reads tenant rows; tenants can look up the platform data the engines use (`GET /threat-intelligence/lookup`) and keep their own allow-lists as BEC trusted senders, DLP exceptions and policy conditions. Prices, invoices and payments: no such data exists (`GET /billing/plan` says `pricing: null`).

**Deferred to later steps.** Archive, journal search, retention policies, legal holds and export: step 8.1. Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace connectors: step 8.2. Deployment manager: step 8.3. Admin-portal screens (webhooks, delivery history, preferences): steps 7.x.

tags.name: threat-intelligence
tags.description: Step 6.1: look up a hash, URL, domain or IP in the platform threat data the engines use (audited, expensive class). Tenant-managed indicators are not offered.

tags.name: webhooks
tags.description: Step 6.2: signed webhook subscriptions (HMAC-SHA256 `EG-Signature`, secret shown once, rotation with overlap), the event catalogue, delivery history with attempts, single and time-range replay, test pings. `webhook:read` / `webhook:manage`; needs the plan feature `webhooks`. Not offered: events for SMTP-time refusals, per-recipient deliveries, URL clicks, DLP incidents and archive (8.1), connector events (8.2), payload version 2, custom headers or mTLS, back-fill of past events; portal screens: 7.x.

tags.name: notifications
tags.description: Step 6.2: tenant security-alert settings (threat detected, DNS record failures, webhook disabled: enabled, severity, throttle windows) and the caller’s own notification preferences (opt-outs, quarantine digest). E-mail only; SMS, chat and push channels are not offered; portal screens: 7.x.

tags.name: platform
tags.description: Platform staff only: overrides (1.3), dead letters (3.2), scan training (4.1), threat hashes and attachment rescans (4.2), threat indicators (4.3), cross-tenant audit log (6.1, users with MFA, audited).

ErrorBody.description: Every error of the API (step 6.1 D1). `code` is a stable snake_case machine code; `message` is a string, or a list of `"<path>: <issue>"` strings for validation errors. Coded errors may add detail fields (ids, states, versions, codes; never content).

code.description: `validation_failed` (unknown fields included), or a specific code such as `cursor_invalid`, `idempotency_key_required`, `idempotency_key_invalid`

X-Request-Id.description: Server-minted id of this request (UUID); quote it when reporting a problem

X-Correlation-Id.description: The caller-supplied x-correlation-id if well formed, otherwise a new one

RateLimit-Limit.description: Requests allowed in the current 60 s window of the most restrictive limit

Idempotency-Replayed.description: `true` when the stored response of an earlier request with the same key is returned
